description: Use this at Step 3 to minimize the human-gated work that stands between "the code is built" and "the project is live and submitted": faucet claims, testnet deploys, burner-wallet creation, provider/API-key signups, and the hackathon submission itself. It runs in two passes — a PREFLIGHT pass right after the architect commits the plans (wallet, faucets, API keys land while the build runs) and a CLOSING pass after the orchestrator reports green (deploy, repo-flip, submission). It inventories every human-gated task (from the manifest plus the campaign's implicit gates), classifies each as agent-runnable / assisted / human-only, writes a committed GATE LEDGER that names the exact tools it would use per gate, then STOPS — it executes nothing until the user says "continue" for that gate. Trigger it ONLY on the user's ask: "run the gates", "preflight the gates", "get the faucets/keys ready", "minimize the human steps", "handle the faucets/deploy/submission", "what's left for me to do", the user starting Step 3 after the orchestrator's offer, or an autopilot dispatch under a locked campaign contract (which counts as the user's start; references/campaign-contract.md). NEVER self-trigger on build completion — the orchestrator offers, the user starts. Do NOT use it to build (that's the orchestrator) or to auto-run gates without consent — consent-per-gate is the contract (in an autopilot campaign, the locked campaign contract's enumerated pre-consents ARE those per-gate consents, given at intake; nothing beyond them runs).
